2019_142_111919regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting held November 19, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. It carries recognitions of Athens photography students and the 2019 Athens boys' soccer state champions, a consent agenda of October 2019 minutes, a first reading of ten board policies, and the September 2019 Treasurer's Report showing total disbursements in the period of $7,641,573.54. Action items ask the board to appoint a negotiating team for the TEA/MEA/NEA contract expiring January 31, 2020 and to award the 2020 roof replacement project to JD Candler and Royal West Roofing for $2,319,975.00 including contingency.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, November 19, 2019, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m.

**Recognitions**
Athens Visual Arts teacher Luba Sordyl and Photography 2 students Katy Ferris, Isabella Sinukto and Nathaniel Adkins; and the 2019 Athens boys' soccer team, MHSAA Division One state champions under coach Todd Heugh, presented by Athletics Director Tim Fulcher. The team won five trophies, finished #1 in Michigan and #13 by the United Soccer Coaches, with 6 All-League, 8 All-District, 4 All-Region and 4 All-State selections. Captains: Davis DiGiovanni, Jason Kemp, Andri Myftari, Donovan Sharp.

**Consent agenda (items A-H)**
Minutes of the October 1, 2019 special meeting, closed session and workshop; the October 15, 2019 special meeting, closed session and regular meeting; a first reading of board policy revisions; and the September 2019 Treasurer's Report. The October 15 minutes record Resolution 19-087 honoring 56 National Merit Semifinalists (Yes 6, No 0, Hammond absent), Resolution 19-089 accepting the Yeo & Yeo audit of the 2018-2019 fiscal year with no material weaknesses, Resolution 19-090 approving NSBA Advocacy Institute attendance in Washington, D.C. February 1-4, 2020, and Resolution 19-091 ratifying a five-member International Academy consortium governing body.

**Board policies - first reading**
| Policy | Title | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1000.01 | Conflict of Interest | Revision |
| 3000.01 | Curriculum Development | Revision |
| 4000.03 | Alcohol and Drug-Free Workplace | Revision |
| 4000.03 | Paid Medical Leave | Addition |
| 4000.03 | Medical Examinations | Revision |
| 4000.05 | Prohibition of Referral or Assistance | Revision |
| 4000.05 | Code of Ethics | Addition |
| 5000.02 | Budget Planning and Adoption | Revision |
| 5000.10 | Fixed Assets | Revision |
| 7000.11 | Volunteers | Addition |

Budget Planning and Adoption keeps the statement that the Board "will endeavor to maintain a minimum year-end general fund balance of fifteen (15) percent." Fixed Assets sets a tracking threshold of items costing more than $5,000 with a useful life exceeding one year. Volunteers requires an ICHAT criminal background check for every volunteer.

**Personnel (item 6.A)**
Appointment of Jordan Harris as chief spokesperson and Rick West, Christine DiPilato, Kris Griffor, Kandice Moynihan, Jessica Carrier and John Pagel as team members for negotiations with the TEA/MEA/NEA, whose contract expires January 31, 2020.

**Meeting and format.** Board of Education regular meeting agenda packet for the Troy School District, Oakland County, Michigan, dated November 19, 2019, 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District address 4400 Livernois, phone 248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Consent agenda items A through H appear at packet p.7, Personnel at p.125 and Business at p.126; Curriculum carried no items.

**Recognitions.** TSD Mission Moment honoring Athens Visual Arts teacher Luba Sordyl and Photography 2 students Katy Ferris, Isabella Sinukto and Nathaniel Adkins. 2019 Athens Boys' Soccer State Champions, presented by Director of Athletics Tim Fulcher: captains Davis DiGiovanni, Jason Kemp, Andri Myftari and Donovan Sharp under head coach Todd Heugh; five trophies including the MHSAA Division One State Championship; 6 All-League, 8 All-District, 4 All-Region and 4 All-State honorees; finished #1 in Michigan and #13 by the United Soccer Coaches.

**October minutes.** The October 1, 2019 special meeting opened at 5:00 p.m. under President Schmidt with Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present and attorney Dana Abrahams of Clark Hill; Resolution 19-085 moved into closed session on attorney-client privilege under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), 5:03 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. The October 1 workshop (6:25-8:07 p.m.) heard the Yeo & Yeo audit report from Taylor Diener and David Youngstrom, a third grade reading and gap analysis, and public comment from Barrington Wilkins. The October 15, 2019 special meeting (6:00 p.m., Hammond absent) adopted Resolution 19-086 for a closed session on negotiations. The October 15 regular meeting began at 7:05 p.m. with roughly 75 audience members and adopted Resolution 19-087 recognizing 56 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists (top one and one-half percent on the PSAT; more than one million entrants from some 22,000 high schools, 16,000 semifinalists), Resolution 19-088 approving the consent agenda including the August 2019 Treasurer's Report, Resolution 19-089 accepting the audited 2019 financial statements, Resolution 19-090 approving Hauff, Gottlieb and Wilson at the NSBA Advocacy Institute in Washington, D.C., February 1-4, 2020, and Resolution 19-091 ratifying a Joint Steering Committee amendment adopted October 2, 2019 creating a five-member governing body of the three Fiscal Agents' representatives plus two at-large members serving two-year terms. All votes were Yes 6, No 0, Hammond absent. George Freeman, computer tech at Hill and Morse Elementary, was honored for re-routing professional learning for 105 teachers to Boulan after Larson Middle School lost power. Board comments noted three Troy schools named National Blue Ribbon Schools and an audit of a $155 million budget without a single correction. Adjourned 8:24 p.m.

**Board policies, first reading (consent item 5.G).** Ten policies from a memo dated Thursday, November 7, 2019 from Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services (4400 Livernois, phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013) to Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky, cc Judy Holmes, based on updates from Lusk and Albertson reviewed by the Policy Committee on Wednesday, October 23, 2019: 1000.01 Conflict of Interest (revision), 3000.01 Curriculum Development (revision, MCL 380.1282(2)), 4000.03 Alcohol and Drug-Free Workplace (revision, federal Drug-Free Workplace Act, 41 USC 8101 et seq., written notice of a criminal drug charge no more than three business days after arraignment), 4000.03 Paid Medical Leave (addition, Michigan Paid Medical Leave Act, MCL 408.961 et seq., enacted December 2018), 4000.03 Medical Examinations (revision, all costs borne by the school district), 4000.05 Prohibition of Referral or Assistance (revision, House Bill 4242 amending MCL 388.1766; districts no longer forfeit $100,000 in state aid but may forfeit 1% of state aid, and personnel in violation are fined no less than 3% of annual compensation), 4000.05 Code of Ethics (addition, Michigan Code of Educational Ethics approved by MDE), 5000.02 Budget Planning and Adoption (revision referencing the most recent applicable GASB requirements after GASB 54 was superseded by GASB 84; budget adopted prior to July 1 each year; minimum year-end general fund balance of fifteen (15) percent), 5000.10 Fixed Assets (revision; items exceeding $5,000 with useful life exceeding one year), and 7000.11 Volunteers (addition requiring Michigan State Police ICHAT checks and barring anyone convicted of a listed offense under MCL 380.1535a or MCL 380.1539b).

**Business, item 8.A - 2020 Roof Replacement Project.** An RFP sought competitive bids for roof replacement at Athens High School, International Academy East and Troy High School and roof restoration at Barnard, Costello and Martell Elementary Schools and the Services Building; bids were reviewed by the TSD Operations Department and WeatherTech Consulting Group. Recommended awards: JD Candler $1,469,500.00 for Athens Roof Area G, IAE Roof Areas B, C, D, E and F and the restorative work; Royal West Roofing $740,000.00 for Troy High Roof Areas A, B, C and D; contingency $110,475.00; total $2,319,975.00, to be approved as an expenditure of the 2019 Capital Projects Fund. A memorandum dated November 6, 2019 from Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance & Operations (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, ph. 248.823.4050) to Rick West, cc Pat Orczykowski, states that Public Bid 9892 resulted in 7 bids, that both low bidders had successfully performed similar work for the district, and that the total roofing work to be completed in 2019 is $2,319,975.00 including a requested 5% contingency. The bid tabulation for "9892 2020 Roof Program" lists JD Candler Roofing, Lutz Roofing, Newton Crane, Royal Roofing, Royal West Roofing, Schena Roofing and Quality Roofing. On the Troy High lump sum (Item 8, Roof Areas A-D), bids were JD Candler $927,000.00, Lutz $897,000.00, Newton Crane $1,074,000.00, Royal Roofing $1,080,600.00, Royal West $740,000.00 at $10.63 per square foot, Schena $1,148,283.00 and Quality $1,103,808.00. On the IAE lump sum (Item 13), JD Candler bid $1,051,700.00, Royal Roofing $1,299,000.00, Royal West $1,018,100.00 with a note that Royal West did not include the addendum items, giving an adjusted total of $1,053,100.00, and Quality $1,158,808.00. On Athens Roof Area G, JD Candler bid $399,000.00 against Lutz $484,650.00, Newton Crane $622,000.00, Royal Roofing $448,120.00, Royal West $448,400.00 and Quality $617,265.00. JD Candler's restoration total for Items 14-17 was $18,800.00.
